title: a quarter circle by x = cos theta
source: WHAT.md, Start here item 1 (consolidation); STAGE0.md S8; DESIGN.md §5.1's canonical reversed case
statement: Evaluate the definite integral of √(1 − x²) from 0 to 1.
notes: x = cos theta is decreasing: the ends are theta = pi/2 (cos(pi/2) = 0) and theta = 0 (cos 0 = 1), checked with the exact values cos_pi_half and cos_zero. The order 0 <= pi/2 is discharged, so int_subst builds the flipped, oriented integral over [0, pi/2] (p1_expected E46).

Installation owes 1 - x^2 >= 0 on [0, 1], closed by the sign product -(x - 1)(x + 1) (E53); the new integrand owes 1 - (cos theta)^2 >= 0, closed as -(cos theta - 1)(cos theta + 1) with cos_le_one and cos_ge_neg_one.
pyth_cos rewrites (cos theta)^2 so that sqrt_sq matches through ring_nf; sqrt_sq then owes sin theta >= 0 on [0, pi/2], closed by cite sin_nonneg_on.
ftc's check is field with pyth_cos as a fact: F' = (1 - cos^2 + sin^2)/2, which is sin^2 once cos^2 is reduced (§6.2's a^k == r).
